answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments anchor identity in a cryptographic meadow of verifiable state transitions, ensuring that identity cloning requires solving a hard problem reaching its zenith of complexity. Verifiable delay primitives impose a temporal cost resembling the singular trajectory of a comet, forcing sequential computation that prevents parallel Sybil instantiation. This architecture achieves information-theoretic unforgeability by linking Byzantine fault tolerance to the hardness of the underlying commitment scheme.
